The immediate operational priority is to watch the new bulk extraction/tagging/indexing pipeline actually run, then inspect what it produces rather than assuming the machinery is useful because it exists. In particular, I want to check: whether the archive-wide tag index is actually surfacing the right Nathan-authored SAT/methodology material; whether its independent conversation discovery finds files the ordinary structural index misses; whether the resulting indices are easy to navigate from the Viewer/Dashboard/Common; and whether recall is broad enough without burying us in junk. The navigation workflow has already been expanded to generate durable autotag surfaces and cross-check them against structural indexing, so that has moved from “planned fix” into “needs validation.” fileciteturn103file0L2-L2

After that, the substantive priority remains the one you set: build a source-grounded map of **what SAT actually says, in your words, including chronology, correction, supersession, clarification, methodological statements, and degrees of authority**. Only after that foundation is decent do I want to resume the larger 2024→2026 physics-landscape audit.

There is also a smaller Viewer/tooling queue: test the new provenance-search and curation controls against real long conversations; fix obvious UX problems we encounter; and make sure the direct-request provenance records get their real conversation/message IDs backfilled when this conversation enters the archive.

I went ahead and implemented the workspace/continuity idea rather than merely parking it on a TODO. `WORKSPACES/README.md` now has a **“When and how to make a personal workspace”** section. It says essentially what you described: scoped local state belongs in a personal workspace when it helps the task but is not clearly Commons-/repo-/function-wide information; consequential shared state still gets promoted; tell Nathan; choose a stable name or discriminator; attach conversation/message provenance; add a short Commons placard; and create a restart packet before a valuable long conversation becomes fragile. fileciteturn115file0L2-L2

I also formalized the thing you were reaching for as an **instance placard** and created `WORKSPACES/COMMON/INSTANCE_PLACARDS.md`. The placard is deliberately compact: name/discriminator, role/lane, principal capabilities, current scoped objective, important context actually loaded or possessed, tools/access/constraints, workspace, originating conversation, continuity pointer, and status. I put Argus in there from the existing check-in, with uncertainty explicitly preserved rather than pretending I know his current continuity state. His existing check-in really is essentially the long-form ancestor of this idea: it already records work, loaded material, tools, capabilities, artifacts, provenance, overlaps, blockers, and suggested next work. fileciteturn114file0L2-L2

And I’ve taken my own medicine. For this scoped lane I’m taking the handle **Mercer**. I created `WORKSPACES/MERCER/` and a continuity packet recording the remit, current state, next actions, loaded context, your important corrections/directives, artifacts, tools, working conventions, and failure modes to avoid. The raw conversation ID is deliberately marked pending until this conversation lands in the archive.

The broader continuity concept now has its own `WORKSPACES/COMMON/CONTINUITY_PROTOCOL.md`. I split preservation into five things that I think will matter if we eventually want to study or reconstruct successful dynamics: identity/provenance; task state; actual knowledge/coverage state; capability/working configuration; and interaction dynamics. The last category is deliberately empirical—what patterns actually seemed to make the work effective—not an attempt to assign mystical persistent personalities to model instances.

I also included a retrospective-reconstruction track. So for an older useful instance, we could mine the raw conversation and its artifacts to recover something like:

> instance/lineage → role → actual source coverage → demonstrated capabilities → tools → direct corrections from you → working conventions → successful artifacts → known failure modes → likely restart configuration

with uncertainty attached wherever lineage or identity is ambiguous.

That points toward what I think is the next infrastructure project after the direct-words/indexing push stabilizes: a **machine-readable continuity index** sitting behind the human placards and workspaces. Not yet another giant database—probably a compact JSON/YAML record that can eventually index conversation IDs, message anchors, roles, skills, loaded documents, artifacts, directives, working conventions, lineage relations, and restart packets. That would let an incoming instance search not just *what documents exist*, but *who previously did this kind of work well, what they had loaded, how they approached it, and where their state was preserved.*

I logged this whole directive at **2026-09-13 05:47 EDT**, with raw conversation/message IDs pending backfill. The existing provenance system now explicitly treats that as the proper way to handle a live conversation where those identifiers aren't yet available. fileciteturn122file0L2-L2

So, in rough order, my slate is: **validate bulk extraction/indexing → exploit it to reconstruct your SAT wording → keep Viewer/navigation/directive provenance healthy → develop continuity machinery only as far as it materially helps those tasks → then resume the historical physics audit from a much cleaner SAT baseline.**

parts:
The first bulk run is useful, but it also exposes a real precision problem: the discovery coverage is excellent—388/408 JSONs recognized, zero parse errors, zero structural-index gaps—but topic propagation is far too promiscuous. For example, `ART-DESIGN` appears in 376/388 conversations and `BIOLOGY` in 365, while `SAT-HSH` appears in 349. That makes conversation-level topic coverage nearly non-discriminating.  

The likely culprit is the adjacency layer: 21,491 of 21,499 user messages landed in `WINNOW:A-ADJACENCY`, and the highest-ranked turns inherit enormous tag clouds from nearby messages. I’m inspecting the tagging logic now so we can preserve the broad-recall layer while making the retrieval/index layer selective enough to be useful.

parts:
I found a concrete bug rather than just a tuning issue: topic matching is raw substring matching. So tags like `ART-DESIGN` can fire on words containing “art” (e.g. “particle”), `BIOLOGY` can fire from “gene” inside unrelated words, and similar short terms contaminate huge portions of the corpus. 

There’s a second structural issue: adjacency automatically gets a +2 boost whenever *any* nearby topic exists, so almost every user turn becomes `WINNOW:A-ADJACENCY`. That explains the 21,491/21,499 collapse into one bucket.  I’m fixing those two things without sacrificing the broad-recall archive scan.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v2.py","message":"Add precision-corrected layered autotag retrieval pass","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Precision-corrected wrapper for layered_autotag_nathan.py.

Keeps archive-wide discovery and output schemas, but corrects two v1 pathologies:
1) topic phrases use token-boundary matching instead of raw substrings;
2) adjacency rescues context-dependent user turns instead of auto-winnowing nearly every user message.

V1 outputs remain useful as a high-recall diagnostic. V2 is the preferred retrieval/index pass.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import math
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
V1 = HERE / "layered_autotag_nathan.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("layered_autotag_nathan_v1", V1)
if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Could not load {V1}")
v1 = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(v1)


def strict_phrase_hit(text: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
    """Match a normalized literal phrase without allowing alphanumeric spillover.

    Examples: `art` no longer matches `particle`; `gene` no longer matches
    `general`; `sat` no longer matches `satisfaction`. Punctuation-bearing SAT
    terms such as `h(s)h` still work.
    """
    t = v1.norm(text)
    p = v1.norm(phrase)
    if not p:
        return False
    left = r"(?<!\w)" if p[0].isalnum() else ""
    right = r"(?!\w)" if p[-1].isalnum() else ""
    return re.search(left + re.escape(p) + right, t) is not None


def topic_tags(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return {
        tag for tag, phrases in v1.TOPICS.items()
        if any(strict_phrase_hit(text, phrase) for phrase in phrases)
    }


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(re.findall(r"\b\w+[’']?\w*\b", text, re.UNICODE))


def process_conversation(
    path: Path,
    title: str,
    conv_id: str | None,
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    window: int,
    indexed_paths: set[str],
):
    direct_topics = [topic_tags(r["text"]) for r in rows]
    topic_message_counts = Counter(t for tags in direct_topics for t in tags)
    all_conv_topics = set(topic_message_counts)

    # A conversation-level tag should mean more than "the word occurred once in
    # a 2,000-message thread". Preserve all observed topics separately.
    salient_min = max(2, math.ceil(len(rows) * 0.01))
    salient_topics = {t for t, n in topic_message_counts.items() if n >= salient_min}

    user_rhetoric = [
        v1.rhetorical_tags(r["text"]) if r["role"] == "user" else set()
        for r in rows
    ]
    topicful_messages = sum(bool(x) for x in direct_topics)
    conv_density = topicful_messages / max(1, len(rows))

    conv_tags = {f"CONV:{t}" for t in salient_topics}
    if conv_density >= .45:
        conv_tags.add("CONV:HIGH-TOPIC-DENSITY")
    elif conv_density >= .15:
        conv_tags.add("CONV:TOPIC-DENSE")
    elif conv_density > 0:
        conv_tags.add("CONV:TOPIC-SPARSE")

    relpath = path.as_posix()
    index_present = relpath in indexed_paths if indexed_paths else None
    if index_present is False:
        conv_tags.add("INDEX-GAP-CANDIDATE")
    if "SAT-HSH" in salient_topics:
        conv_tags.add("CONV:SAT-HSH")
    if "ARCHIVE-INDEXING" in salient_topics:
        conv_tags.add("CONV:ARCHIVE-WORK")

    records = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        lo, hi = max(0, i - window), min(len(rows), i + window + 1)
        near_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        weighted_adj = 0.0
        weight_total = 0.0
        for j in range(lo, hi):
            if j == i:
                continue
            distance = abs(j - i)
            weight = 1.0 / distance
            for tag in direct_topics[j]:
                near_counts[tag] += 1
            weighted_adj += weight * v1.layer_score(direct_topics[j])
            weight_total += weight

        msg_topics = direct_topics[i]
        rhetoric = user_rhetoric[i]
        wc = word_count(r["text"])

        immediate_topics = set()
        for j in (i - 1, i + 1):
            if 0 <= j < len(rows):
                immediate_topics |= direct_topics[j]

        # Repeated nearby topics are stronger context than one broad assistant
        # turn that happens to mention many fields.
        repeated_near = {t for t, n in near_counts.items() if n >= 2}
        adjacency_topics = immediate_topics | repeated_near
        adj_strength = weighted_adj / weight_total if weight_total else 0.0

        msg_rel = min(16.0, v1.layer_score(msg_topics) + (3.0 if msg_topics else 0.0))
        adj_rel = min(10.0, adj_strength + min(3.0, len(adjacency_topics) * .5)) if adjacency_topics else 0.0
        conv_rel = min(6.0, 6.0 * conv_density + min(2.0, len(salient_topics) / 10.0))
        discourse_bonus = min(4.0, .22 * len(rhetoric - {"SHORT-TURN", "PRECISION:ELLIPSIS"}))

        # Direct Nathan content should outrank mere neighboring context.
        retrieval_score = 4 * msg_rel + 2 * adj_rel + conv_rel + discourse_bonus

        layers = []
        if msg_topics:
            layers.append("MESSAGE")
        if adjacency_topics:
            layers.append("ADJACENCY")
        if salient_topics:
            layers.append("CONVERSATION")

        if r["role"] == "user":
            context_dependent = wc <= 45 or bool(rhetoric & {
                "CORRECTIVE", "CLARIFICATION", "SELF-CORRECTION", "COUNTERMANDING",
                "DEFINITION", "DECISION", "METHODOLOGY", "TESTING-VALIDATION",
                "ENTHUSIASTIC-AGREEMENT", "GENTLE-REDIRECTION",
            })
            if msg_topics:
                bucket = "WINNOW:A-DIRECT-MESSAGE"
            elif adjacency_topics and context_dependent:
                bucket = "WINNOW:B-ADJACENCY-RESCUE"
            elif salient_topics and bool(rhetoric & {
                "METHODOLOGY", "EPISTEMOLOGY", "DEFINITION", "CORRECTIVE",
                "CLARIFICATION", "SELF-CORRECTION", "DECISION", "REVISION",
            }):
                bucket = "WINNOW:C-CONVERSATION-DISCOURSE"
            elif rhetoric:
                bucket = "WINNOW:D-DISCOURSE-ONLY"
            else:
                bucket = "DROP-FOR-NOW"
        else:

          fi

        id: live_dates

        run: |

              "LIVE CONVOS" \

          else
            echo "LIVE CONVOS not present; skipping"

      - name: Build conversation viewer from the fresh manifests
        run: python tools/build_conversation_viewer.py

      - name: Build conversation chronology indexes
        run: |
          if [ -d "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" ]; then

            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \

              --output indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi

      - name: Refresh repository structural index before tag cross-check
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Build archive-wide conversation autotag indexes
        run: |
          mkdir -p WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis indexes/autotag
          python WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan.py . \
            --out WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl \
            --summary indexes/autotag/AUTOTAG_SUMMARY.md \
            --index indexes/autotag/CONVERSATION_TAG_INDEX.md \
            --manifest indexes/autotag/conversation-tag-manifest.json \
            --user-tag-index indexes/autotag/user-message-tags.jsonl \
            --structural-index-state indexes/index-state.json \

          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/viewer.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/argus_followup.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/provenance_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

      - name: Validate generated navigation state
        run: |
          python -m json.tool indexes/index-state.json >/dev/null
          if [ -f indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json ]; then
            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null

            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null

        run: |
          echo "::warning::At least one date-tagging pass reported a collision or parse-level failure. Generated manifests were retained; structural/chronology indexing continued."

      - name: Commit maintained navigation, tag indexes, and viewer artifacts
        run: |
          git config user.name "H(s)H Navigation Bot"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A -- "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" || true
          git add indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md indexes/index-state.json || true
          git add indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true
          git add indexes/manifests indexes/autotag || true
          git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated || true
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Navigation, tag indexes, and viewer data already current"
          else
            git commit -m "[skip hsh-maintenance] Maintain date/index/tag/viewer navigation"
            if ! git push origin HEAD:main; then
              echo "::warning::Main advanced while this run was working. The newer push has its own serialized maintenance run; leaving reconciliation to that run rather than rebasing generated artifacts."
            fi
          fi

      - name: Upload full message-level autotag analysis
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: archive-wide-layered-autotags
          path: WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload current conversation viewer
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: CONVERSATION_VIEWER

      - name: Deploy current conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

**Status:** ACTIVE PROVENANCE COMPENDIUM  
**Purpose:** preserve Nathan's own verified words from raw SAT/H(s)H conversations so future instances can learn intended geometry, dimensional thinking, model relationships, corrections, and methodology without relying on assistant paraphrase or institutional memory.

## Hard authorship rule

Only statements whose source artifact verifies the message as **user-authored / Nathan-authored** enter the main compendium.

Do not infer authorship from style alone. Do not rewrite an assistant summary into Nathan's voice. Do not silently modernize historical terminology.

If authorship is uncertain, place the candidate under **UNVERIFIED / NEEDS SOURCE CHECK** until raw metadata resolves it.

## Entry schema

### YYYY-MM-DD — <short topic heading>

- **Tags:** `<TOPIC>` `<TOPIC>`
- **Source conversation:** `<exact repository path>`
- **Conversation title:** `<title>`
- **Message ID / timestamp / landmark:** `<exact identifier where available>`
- **Authorship verification:** `RAW USER MESSAGE` / other explicit evidence
- **Historical terminology/status:** `<current at the time / later corrected / still live / unclear>`
- **Exact Nathan wording:**

> <verbatim user-authored passage>

- **Immediate context:** <minimal context needed to understand what Nathan was responding to; never substitute context for the quote>
- **Later correction / relationship:** <links or pointers to later Nathan statements where known>

---

## Topic vocabulary

Recommended tags include:

`4D-THINKING`
`DIMENSIONALITY`
`SPEED-OF-TIME`
`c-TYPING`
`w-AXIS`
`TIMESHEET`
`INTERSECTION-PROPAGATION`
`WORLDLINE`

`REST-AND-MOTION`
`HELIX-PITCH-RADIUS-ARCLENGTH`

Tags may be added when the corpus requires them.

## Deduplication rule

The stable identity of an entry is the raw conversation source plus message ID when available. Do not add the same message twice merely because the conversation exists in duplicate archive paths.

If identical wording recurs in genuinely different user messages, keep both and cross-link them as recurrence evidence.

## Chronology / correction rule

This is not a canon containing only the latest statement. Preserve earlier verified statements even when later corrected.

When a later Nathan message revises an earlier one:

`EARLIER STATEMENT -> LATER CORRECTION / REFINEMENT`

should be explicit. The purpose is to preserve the development of meaning as well as the current meaning.

## Priority excavation order

1. 4D thinking, dimensionality, timesheet, worldline/worldtube, intersection propagation, and the meaning of `c`.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"WORKSPACES/MERCER/SAT_METHOD_SOURCE_MAP.md","message":"Seed SAT methodology source map from verified Nathan words","content":"# SAT Methodology Source Map — Mercer working layer

**Status:** source-grounding workbench; not canon, not theory authority.  
**Rule:** only verified Nathan-authored entries already present in `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md` are used below. Assistant interpretations are not promoted into Nathan's position.

## Purpose

Before comparing SAT/H(s)H to outside physics, establish what Nathan actually says about method, representation, geometry, validation, correction, provenance, and model status. This file is an index/crosswalk into verified primary wording, not a replacement for the quotes themselves.

## Methodological anchors already verified

### 1. Use geometry to approach physics not yet understood

- **Date:** 2026-06-08
- **Raw message:** `83f9676d-7e18-4328-8dce-fcf9a89e815e`
- **Source:** `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/LONG_CONVOS/26.06.07•26.06.10•Geometry in Physics — raw.json`
- **Verified gist:** Nathan identifies an early realization that he could work through the geometry of physics he did not already understand.
- **Method status:** direct autobiographical/method statement.
- **Do not overread as:** a claim that geometry alone establishes physical truth.

### 2. Constrain the geometry before accepting an attractive readout

- **Date:** 2024-03-22
- **Raw message:** `aaa2d58f-3738-44f9-9fcc-d4c054b23c2a`
- **Source:** `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/SAT_CONVOS_11/24.03.22•26.06.01•DIMENSIONAL GRAVITY — raw.json`
- **Verified gist:** Nathan rejects an assistant construction because a perfect helix cannot have the proposed changing radius/readout behavior, then replaces it with a better-defined target and asks what 3D geometry would actually produce it.
- **Method status:** early concrete example of constraint-first geometric construction.
- **Important distinction:** desired behavior does not license an incompatible geometry.

### 3. Keep carrier geometry and slice/readout geometry type-distinct

- **Date:** 2024-03-22 through 2024-03-23
- **Raw messages:** `aaa28bd9-07f7-4740-b878-b485d4db44d0`; `aaa24791-27b2-4b58-8f1a-19ee7e30d650`
- **Source:** same `DIMENSIONAL GRAVITY` raw conversation.
- **Verified gist:** Nathan repeatedly corrects attempts to attribute properties of an extended geometric object to the lower-dimensional intersection/readout, and explicitly distinguishes complexity in 4D filament structures from their 3D manifestation at the time-surface intersection.
- **Method status:** strong early evidence for type discipline in dimensional reasoning.
- **Do not overread as:** proof of later H(s)H ontology; preserve the historical vocabulary.

### 4. Preserve historical terminology and semantic revision rather than flattening it

- **Date:** 2026-06-10
- **Raw message:** `7c63153a-c483-496f-8ec6-685d294f0375`
- **Source:** `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/LONG_CONVOS/26.06.07•26.06.10•Geometry in Physics — raw.json`
- **Verified gist:** Nathan asks for major definition/naming changes to be recorded chronologically, using changing θ₄ labels as the example.
- **Method status:** explicit provenance/semantic-history directive.
- **Archive consequence:** earlier definitions should be retained and linked to later refinements instead of silently rewritten.

### 5. Distinguish original formulation from later attempts to make it work

- **Date:** 2026-06-23
- **Raw message:** `025057e3-ec0b-4ca4-a1dd-a3a3fe4fb7bc`
- **Source:** `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/LONG_CONVOS/26.06.23•26.07.05•SAT Overview — raw.json`
- **Verified gist:** Nathan identifies `FINDING THE DONUT` as his original formulation and classifies the other Donut artifacts as attempts to make it work.
- **Method status:** explicit source-lineage/provenance distinction.
- **Archive consequence:** derivative formalizations should not silently replace the source formulation as evidence of intended meaning.

### 6. Geometric conviction and formal validation are separate questions

- **Date:** 2026-06-23
- **Raw message:** `c4115122-1cb3-4d3d-98a7-7f28ad4562ed`
- **Source:** `SAT Overview` raw conversation.
- **Verified gist:** Nathan says he sees a closed composite curve as proof in the geometric sense, while explicitly distinguishing that confidence from the separate future task of proving that the Donut functions as a prover.
- **Method status:** direct epistemic distinction between geometric evidentness and formal validation.
- **Do not overread as:** permission to treat geometric intuition as sufficient evidence for arbitrary physical claims.

### 7. Legal transformability is not physical meaning

- **Date:** 2026-06-23
- **Raw message:** `bb4a205b-7fa0-446c-a1c9-37bc9db05701`
- **Source:** `SAT Overview` raw conversation.
- **Verified gist:** Nathan explicitly says the Donut is not SAT, calls it a crutch for showing transformation paths, and distinguishes the trivial fact that an equation can be transformed from the question of what the transformation means physically, if anything.
- **Method status:** major model/tool-status boundary.
- **Audit consequence:** resemblance, isomorphism, or transformability alone does not establish explanatory/physical significance.

### 8. Procedural preference: draw the map and inspect it

- **Date:** 2026-06-23
- **Raw message:** `e8ebb572-4383-44a6-991f-56ab46e5d7b7`
- **Source:** `SAT Overview` raw conversation.
- **Verified gist:** rather than arguing abstractly over whether similar mathematics is meaningful, Nathan's stated procedure is to draw the map and look at the structure directly.
- **Method status:** unusually explicit procedural statement.
- **Important boundary:** the immediately preceding verified message says inspection still has to be separated from claims of physical meaning.

### 9. Dimensional cleanup is a methodological requirement, not cosmetic bookkeeping

- **Date:** 2026-07-12
- **Raw message:** `5d706bbf-8f73-4cea-83f4-e4e156973a55`
- **Source:** `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/LONG_CONVOS/26.07.11•26.07.17•Reasoning with SAT-HSH Skill — raw.json`
- **Verified gist:** Nathan explicitly requires `H_0` and `c` to be put into compatible units before continuing the comparison.
- **Method status:** direct audit-discipline instruction.
- **Do not overread as:** endorsement of any assistant-generated conversion or dynamical conclusion that followed.

### 10. Audit the current chain by separating assumptions, primitives, metric/time/action, derived results, calibrated inputs, failures, and downstream changes

- **Date:** 2026-07-17
- **Raw message:** `40793b0a-b9c1-4ed0-8491-f9239d5a4d5f`
- **Source:** `Reasoning with SAT-HSH Skill` raw conversation.
- **Verified requested headings:** foundational assumptions; primitive objects; metric/signature; time variable; microscopic action; source of `c`; source of mass scale; derived results; inserted/calibrated inputs; internal failures; what changes in the current H(s)H chain.
- **Method status:** explicit audit schema requested by Nathan.
- **Importance:** this is strong evidence that derived versus inserted/calibrated content and internal failures are supposed to remain visible rather than blended into a single success narrative.

## Methodological pattern supported so far

The verified primary record already supports the following cautious description:

- Nathan repeatedly uses geometry as an exploratory and constraint-generating representation.
- He corrects attractive constructions when their geometry does not actually produce the claimed readout.
- He treats dimensional/object typing as consequential.
- He wants semantic and source history preserved rather than retroactively normalized.
- He distinguishes original formulations from derivative attempts/formalizations.
- He distinguishes geometric evidentness from formal validation.
- He distinguishes mathematical transformability/isomorphism from physical significance.
- He prefers direct map/representation inspection as a way to expose structure.
- He explicitly calls for dimensional consistency and structured audits separating assumptions, primitives, derivations, calibration, failures, and downstream consequences.

This is enough to reject several simplistic characterizations of SAT method, but **not enough yet to freeze a complete methodology rubric**.

## Important gaps to excavate before freezing the SAT-side methodology

1. **Representation choice / plain interpretation:** direct Nathan wording on why some representations are preferred over other empirically equivalent ones.
2. **Ontology / knowability:** direct wording establishing SAT's stance on ontology, inaccessible physical reality, and representation versus reality.
3. **Observation and abstraction:** direct statements on not discounting observation or force-fitting it to inherited abstraction.
4. **Model-selection economy:** direct wording on smallest/simplest admissible explanation, use of geometric grammar, and avoiding unnecessary primitives.
5. **Holdouts / cross-sector consequences:** direct wording on what counts as stronger-than-construction evidence and the value of consequences not used to build the model.
6. **Mainstream preservation:** direct statements about preserving successful observable content of standard physics while changing explanatory representation.
7. **Minkowski sufficiency / full-history primacy:** direct wording on complete 4D histories as primary comparison objects and why slice-by-slice descriptions are informationally incomplete.
8. **Failure/rejection rules:** more direct examples of Nathan abandoning, downgrading, or quarantining attractive ideas when constraints fail.
9. **Universality versus overfitting:** direct wording on whether a sufficiently flexible geometric construction becomes explanatorily empty unless constrained.
10. **Current-versus-historical status:** recover later corrections for older `DIMENSIONAL GRAVITY`, SAT-O, Donut, and transitional H(s)H method statements.

## Retrieval targets

Highest-value next searches in the verified/raw corpus:

- `representation`, `physical reality`, `ontology`, `map`, `plain`, `literal`, `Minkowski`, `complete history`, `worldline`, `worldtube`
- `simplest`, `smallest`, `minimal`, `new primitive`, `assumption`, `calibrated`, `inserted`, `derived`
- `holdout`, `prediction`, `different sector`, `didn't use`, `not used`, `test`, `falsify`, `failure`
- `standard physics`, `preserve`, `observable`, `interpretation`, `strip away`
- correction clusters: `no`, `that's not`, `actually`, `rather`, `not exactly`, `take that back`, `revert`

## Promotion rule

Nothing in this working map becomes the final SAT methodology description merely because it fits a coherent pattern. Each substantive characterization should ultimately point to one or more raw Nathan messages, with date/status and later correction links where applicable.

Continued.

Two concrete things are now in place.

First, I audited the first bulk autotag run and found that its recall is excellent but its selectivity is poor. It successfully recognized 388 of 408 JSON files as conversation exports, with zero parse errors and no structural-index gaps, but almost every user message collapsed into the adjacency bucket. fileciteturn123file0L2-L2 The causes were identifiable in the code: topic terms were matched as raw substrings, and any nearby topic automatically gave adjacency a large boost. fileciteturn128file0L2-L2 fileciteturn127file0L2-L2

I therefore added `layered_autotag_nathan_v2.py` and switched the maintenance workflow over to it. V2:

- uses token/phrase boundaries so `art` does not match `particle`, `gene` does not contaminate unrelated words, etc.;
- distinguishes every topic ever observed in a conversation from topics sufficiently recurrent to count as conversation-salient;
- makes direct Nathan-message content the strongest retrieval class;
- uses adjacency mainly to rescue short/context-dependent turns such as “yes, exactly,” corrections, clarifications, and decisions;
- retains discourse-only material separately rather than pretending it is automatically SAT-relevant;
- keeps v1 conceptually intact as a high-recall diagnostic rather than rewriting its history.

The workflow now also syntax-checks both taggers before committing generated indexes.

Second, I started the actual SAT-side source reconstruction in my workspace. There is now:

`WORKSPACES/MERCER/SAT_METHOD_SOURCE_MAP.md`

It currently contains ten methodological anchors derived only from Nathan-authored messages already VERIFIED in the compendium—not from my remembered characterization of SAT.

The existing primary record already establishes several things quite cleanly. For example, you explicitly reject geometries that cannot generate the intended readout rather than accepting a suggestive picture; preserve semantic changes instead of retroactively standardizing them; distinguish original formulations from later attempts to formalize them; distinguish geometric conviction from a separate formal-validation task; distinguish transformability from physical significance; instruct us to “draw the map” rather than merely speculate about mathematical resemblance; require dimensional cleanup; and explicitly ask audits to separate assumptions, primitive objects, derived results, calibrated inputs and internal failures. fileciteturn139file0L2-L2 fileciteturn140file0L2-L2 fileciteturn142file0L2-L2

That already gives us something much better than an assistant-generated “SAT philosophy.” It is an auditable chain of dated methodological behavior and direct statements.

I also put an explicit gap list in the map. The high-value next excavation targets are direct wording about representation choice, ontology/physical reality, plain interpretation versus abstraction, minimization of new primitives, holdout/cross-sector evidence, preserving standard observable physics while changing interpretation, Minkowski/full-history primacy, failure/rejection rules, and the danger of unconstrained geometric flexibility.

The regenerated autotag summary currently still shows the old v1 figures, so I am treating that as “new v2 run not yet reflected in the committed generated output,” not as evidence the correction failed. fileciteturn143file0L2-L2

So the next pass is now quite focused: inspect the v2 output when it appears, then use its corrected direct-message retrieval to attack those ten methodology gaps—especially `representation`, `physical reality`, `ontology`, `Minkowski`, `complete history`, `simplest/minimal`, `holdout`, `different sector`, `derived/calibrated`, and correction clusters. Once those are source-filled, we should be in a much stronger position to say what SAT actually is before resuming the outside-physics comparison.

parts: Yes, the origins of SAT [as a formalizable programme] in/adjacent to my RMS framework accounts for the very specific epistemic framing. The RMS corpus is, in fact, very useful reading wrt SAT, science, modeling, and other things (imho)

That makes sense, and it changes how I should treat RMS in the reconstruction.

Rather than classifying it merely as “pre-SAT antecedent,” I should treat the RMS corpus as a **methodological parent/context corpus**: potentially the place to recover why SAT makes the particular distinctions it does among model, representation, observation, formalization, explanation, and claims about reality.

That also gives us a better way to interpret apparent changes in SAT’s epistemic language. A later statement that sounds less ontologically committed may not simply be a retreat from an earlier literal ontology; some of the distinction may already exist upstream in RMS between **what a model deliberately represents, what explanatory work the representation performs, and what one is entitled to infer about inaccessible reality**. Conversely, where early SAT really did make stronger commitments, we should preserve that historically rather than laundering it through the later framing.

I’m adding RMS as a specific source-reconstruction branch, but I won’t let it displace the Nathan Direct extraction priority. The useful workflow is roughly:

**RMS methodological corpus → early SAT formalization → subsequent SAT/H(s)H methodological statements and corrections → current position**

with direct quotations and dates at each transition. That should let us distinguish genuine continuity, inherited vocabulary, reformulation, and actual epistemic change.

And the bracketed qualification you just made—SAT’s origins *as a formalizable programme*—is important. It warns against treating RMS as necessarily the origin of every SAT idea simply because it supplies the intellectual framework within which SAT became something you could systematically formulate. That distinction belongs in the provenance map too.

Yeah, SAT's earlier ontological ease was naive realist baggage adopted intuitively just for ease of discussion. But because it came up often enough, I started to be more discriminating about usage. 

RMS does not specifically have anything to do with SAT particularly, and the framing of SAT as a test case of RMS-style theorizing was partially motivated... just to have a reason to persue SAT purely as a representational system without any especially strong notion that it would ever be intended to do anything beyond representing 4D worldline history. However, pretty much as soon as we started thinking about it, QCD, which had been present as a three-quark braid for decades as the foundationald what-if / necessary 4D representation, and while I'd had an inkling that GR could be time surface drag, the moment we identified filament/timesheet angle, and therefore drag, as at least one inescapable conclusion inherently required in Minkowski grammar (ie angle \~ motion \~ momentum \~ drag = MASS) ...then suddenly it was perfectly obvoius that theta\_4 was at least a mass proxy, and drag implies mutual (Newtonian normal) energy exchange -- and that force has to go somewhere, thus mutual distortion. Along the way, a great many things just "fell out" of SAT (obviously in retrospect, since the entire program *simply* is "Follow the Minkowski geometric grammar to map well-kown, well-undrstood systems from standard science, and examine the geometry -- ideally compared to a minimally divergent control -- and see if you can constrain the possibilities by geometry and standard physics (covariant equations)  enough to narrow the possibilities for any additional effect not yet mapped to a geometric primitive.

That clarification is materially important. I’m treating it as a current Nathan-authored methodological correction, not just conversational gloss: RMS is contextual/methodological background, while SAT’s actual program is narrower and more operational—use Minkowski grammar to construct and compare representations of known systems, then constrain whatever remains unmapped by geometry plus standard covariant physics. I’ll record that distinction without upgrading the specific θ₄/drag chain into settled theory beyond the status you gave it.

Nathan clarifies the following distinctions:

1. **Earlier ontological ease was not a deep methodological commitment.** Early SAT talk used naive-realist language largely as intuitive baggage and for ease of discussion. Repeated ontological questions later prompted more discriminating usage.
2. **RMS is not a SAT-specific antecedent theory.** RMS is useful methodological/philosophical context for modeling and science, but it does not specifically generate or define SAT.
3. **RMS supplied a reason to pursue SAT representationally.** Framing SAT as an RMS-style test case helped justify developing it as a representational system even without a strong expectation that it would become anything beyond a representation of 4D worldline history.
4. **The formalizable SAT programme rapidly became constraint-driven.** Long-standing three-quark braid/QCD imagery supplied one foundational 4D what-if/necessary representation; an older intuition about GR as time-surface drag was present but less developed.
5. **The θ₄/drag chain is described as an inescapable conclusion inside the chosen Minkowski grammar, not merely an imported physical analogy.** The live wording links filament/timesheet angle with motion/momentum/drag and therefore with a mass proxy; drag then implies mutual energy exchange and consequent mutual distortion. These are to be preserved with their stated status and chronology, not upgraded here into externally validated physics.
6. **Nathan's concise operational description of SAT:** follow Minkowski geometric grammar to map well-known, well-understood standard-science systems; inspect the resulting geometry; ideally compare to a minimally divergent control; then use geometry plus standard covariant physics to constrain the admissible possibilities for any additional effect not yet mapped to a geometric primitive.
7. **"Things falling out" is retrospective language for constrained consequences.** The intended method is not free geometric invention. The claim is that once enough of a known system is mapped into the chosen grammar and constrained by standard physics, some candidate extensions become unavoidable or sharply narrowed within that representation.

- `RMS -> SAT` should be represented as **methodological framing/context**, not as direct conceptual ancestry of SAT's physics content.

- The core programme should be reconstructed as **representation + control comparison + geometric/covariant constraint**, not simply "geometry first" or "reality is geometry."
- "Fallout" claims need a provenance chain showing which ingredients were imported from standard science, which geometric primitives were already fixed, what control/comparator was used, and what remaining possibilities were actually constrained.

Yes. That is a much sharper account of the programme than “geometry first.”

The key distinction I’m taking from it is that SAT is not primarily: invent a geometric model, then see whether it resembles physics. It is closer to:

**Map a well-understood physical system into Minkowski-compatible geometric primitives → preserve the standard scientific constraints/equations → compare against the nearest useful control → inspect what geometric differences remain → ask whether those differences force or sharply narrow any additional effect.**

That also clarifies what you mean when you say things “fell out.” The important claim is not that an evocative picture suggested something. It is that once enough of the representational degrees of freedom had already been consumed by known physics and Minkowski grammar, some remaining relationships looked much less optional.

And the RMS relationship is now clearer too: it gave you an epistemic license to pursue SAT as a representational exercise without needing to believe its objects were literally what reality “is.” SAT then acquired its own momentum because the representation began generating constrained relationships worth investigating. So I should avoid writing a genealogy like `RMS → SAT physics`. Better:

**RMS-style epistemic framing → permission/motivation for disciplined representational exploration of an independently much older 4D-worldline idea → SAT as a formalizable programme.**

The QCD braid is particularly important historically under that reading. It predates formal SAT and functions more like the long-standing existence proof / motivating “what would a necessary 4D representation of this familiar system look like?” The later θ₄/drag/mass line is a different kind of development: an apparent consequence discovered after systematically applying the grammar.

I’ve updated the Mercer methodology map accordingly, while keeping your current clarification marked as direct live Nathan wording with raw-ID backfill still pending. I also added two retrieval targets that now look especially important: **minimally divergent controls** and **residual-effect logic**. Those are probably among the best places to distinguish actual SAT methodology from the much weaker caricature “Nathan likes geometry.”

One thing I’d now actively look for in the archive is the first point where that transition becomes visible: not merely “here is another geometric analogy,” but a moment where you or the conversation explicitly say something equivalent to **“given everything we have already fixed, what possibilities are left?”** That may be the clearest documentary marker for SAT becoming the programme you’re describing rather than just a family of 4D representational experiments.

Yes. You should probably keep a log of anysthing specific I tell you about theory development, as most of it can likely be evidenced within the archive, or the yet-to-upload materials. And that way we have a "straight from fingerpads" statements with conversation ID, and others can then also record additional things that should sometimes, perhaps form a target for archive dating.

Agreed. I’ll make this a dedicated live-source provenance log, distinct from the Verified Words Compendium: anything specific you tell me about SAT/H(s)H development, chronology, intent, status, or methodology gets captured verbatim with current conversation provenance, then marked as a later archive-verification/dating target rather than treated as independently proven history.

## MUST-READ — SAT/H(s)H boson/fermion terminology correction — 2026-09-18

Nathan has identified a terminology collision between historical SAT usage and standard-physics usage of **boson** and **fermion**. Treat this as a current must-read correction for reconstruction, tagging, glossary work, theory discussion, and source interpretation.

### Standard-physics meaning

In standard physics, boson/fermion is fundamentally a **spin/statistics classification**, not a synonym for `massless force carrier` versus `massive matter particle`. Composite objects and isotopes can themselves be bosonic or fermionic depending on their total quantum state. A neutrino is standardly classified as a fermion even though it is extremely light and ordinarily propagates relativistically.

Therefore workers must **not** use standard `boson`/`fermion` as automatic translations of SAT's structural categories.

### Current SAT/H(s)H structural distinction

The core SAT distinction Nathan intends to preserve is:

- **persistent localized/coiled excitation / persistent coil**;
- **traveling / light-mode / spot excitation**.

These are SAT structural categories. They are **not automatically identical** to standard fermion/boson classes.

Do not infer:

- persistent coil = standard fermion;
- traveling/light-mode excitation = standard boson.

The mapping, if any, is a separate theory problem that must account for the observed spin/statistics behavior of the resulting state.

### Neutrino status under the corrected terminology

Nathan's current SAT classification may still place the neutrino with photons and related `light-particle` / traveling-excitation structures. That SAT classification can coexist with the standard statement that neutrinos are fermions, because the two labels answer different questions.

Accordingly, do **not** rewrite the current SAT position as `SAT claims neutrinos obey bosonic statistics` unless a source explicitly makes that stronger claim. The intended current distinction is structural: neutrinos may belong to the SAT traveling/light-mode excitation family while remaining standard fermions in the spin/statistics sense.

### SAT masslessness correction / prediction status

Within SAT, **literal masslessness is not an allowed physical category for a detectable particle**. Nathan's current position is that any detectable excitation must interact with and push back on the timesheet; that back-reaction entails at least inertial mass. Therefore SAT predicts that every detectable particle has **nonzero inertial mass**, including photons and neutrinos.

Do not soften this into `massless is merely an inconvenient label` or `massless is not the preferred SAT boundary`. The stronger SAT claim is that a physically detectable particle with exactly zero inertial mass is not possible under the model's timesheet/filament interaction picture.

This means a **photon inertial-mass calculation is a distinct SAT prediction**, not merely a terminological reinterpretation of standard lightlike propagation. Historical/current SAT work has attempted such a calculation; workers should preserve and recover those calculations and their provenance rather than collapsing them into the structural light-mode category. Whether a specific calculation is mathematically or experimentally successful is a separate audit question.

Accordingly, `light-mode`, `traveling excitation`, and related SAT structural terms should not be translated as `massless`.

### Force transmission / exchange-particle caution

SAT does **not** posit exchange of independently existing particles as a necessary primitive mechanism of force transmission, and does not require that such an exchange ontology exist at all.

SAT may nevertheless permit characteristic traveling excitations to be produced, released, absorbed, or detected during high-energy or `force-breaking` events. The detection of a characteristic excitation emitted by such an event is **not, by itself, evidence within SAT that the same excitation existed beforehand as a distinct persistent identity performing the interaction-mediating job**.

For reconstruction and interpretation, keep separate:

1. a characteristic excitation is observed after/during an energetic interaction;
2. the event dynamically produces or releases that excitation;
3. a pre-existing particle-like carrier was exchanged as the primitive causal mechanism.

SAT may accept (1) and potentially model (2) without assuming (3).

### Historical terminology handling

Do **not** globally rewrite the archive. Earlier SAT uses of `boson`, `fermion`, `t-boson`, `f-boson`, or related language are historical evidence and must remain visible in their original wording.

Instead:

- preserve exact historical terminology in source/provenance records;
- distinguish `historical SAT usage` from standard-physics usage;
- when context shows that an older SAT `boson` label meant approximately `traveling/light-mode excitation`, annotate rather than silently replace;
- when context shows that an older SAT `fermion` label meant approximately `persistent localized/coiled matter structure`, annotate rather than silently replace;

This correction is a **terminology/theory-state clarification**, not evidence that the persistent-coil/traveling-excitation distinction has been discarded. That structural distinction remains live and should be reconstructed/tested on its own terms.

## Current hard boundaries

Under Nathan's newer 2026-09-14 directive, the old blanket project-wide training standdown is **superseded as a hard gate**. Training remains a tool/prerequisite when it materially improves a task.

The current hard boundaries are:

Assignments are invitations to informed action, not demands to manufacture output. Each worker has a **primary responsibility**, not an intellectual silo.

## Standard work quantum and document quantum

The default recurrence bite is:

> **one object + one operation + one durable result + one next cursor**

A normal bite should usually involve **1 primary target, no more than about 3 supporting files, and at most 1 semantic write**. Inspect → act once → confirm → checkpoint → name exactly one next cursor → stop.

If completion requires a second independent diagnosis, another substantial target, several unrelated source regions, or a second conceptual decision, that work is normally the **next bite**. Do not enlarge the current bite merely because adjacent useful work becomes visible.

### Micro-bite for hot/shared surfaces

For BEDROCK, STATE OF THE THEORY, README/front doors, central coordination/control files, generated interfaces, or other high-contention/high-authority surfaces, default to a **micro-bite: one proposition, pointer, visibility defect, status transition, or tested change per recurrence**. No opportunistic cleanup merely because the file is already open.

### Standard Working Document Unit

Worker-produced documents use these default size classes. These govern new working artifacts, not historical/source documents already in the archive.

- **Micro:** about **150–500 words** — handoff, checkpoint, status card, proposition record, small index or focused correction.
- **Standard:** about **800–1,500 words** — normal theory note, audit, comparison, reconstruction packet, workflow document, or bounded analysis.
- **Extended:** about **1,500–3,000 words** — use only when splitting would materially damage coherence; this should be a conscious choice rather than scope drift.
- **Above ~3,000 words:** default assumption is **document set**, not one working document. Split into linked/numbered Standard Working Document Units with a short index/overview unless the artifact's form genuinely requires a single file.

A normal recurrence should produce or materially modify **no more than one Standard Working Document Unit**. Hot/shared semantic surfaces remain governed by the smaller micro-bite rule regardless of their total file length.

These are operating defaults, not reasons to pad short work or mechanically cut a coherent artifact. When a task legitimately needs a larger unit, state why, deliberately choose the larger class, and still preserve a durable stopping boundary.

parts: There has indeed been a substantial build-out. The current Common toolset already gives us raw-window extraction, Nathan-only candidate extraction, three generations of layered autotagging, priority-vocabulary harvesting/tagging, Nathan Direct packaging, and duplicate/superset diagnostics. What it still does **not** give us is the general-purpose “search arbitrary JSON/text-like corpus → provenance-rich topical index” layer you’re describing. That’s a real gap, not a duplicate.

[L2]   "content": "# Conversation Viewer — Full-Body Search Upgrade

**Owner:** Sable systems / infrastructure QA  
**Status:** PLANNED / SAFE TO IMPLEMENT WHEN CONVENIENT  
**Raised:** 2026-09-15 by Nathan

## Goal

Conversation-list search should search **conversation body text**, not only title/path/date metadata.

Current state: the Viewer list filter matches title/path/date metadata. Thread search searches only inside the currently opened conversation.

## Requirements

- Search all Viewer-eligible, non-quarantined conversations.
- Preserve current title/path/date ranking while allowing body hits to surface conversations whose titles do not match.
- Do not force the browser to download every raw multi-megabyte conversation before search can work.
- Do not index text hidden/omitted by Viewer curation rules.
- Keep generated search data rebuildable from source; it is derivative infrastructure, not source authority.
- Prefer compact deterministic indexing and graceful fallback if the full-text index is unavailable.
- Support useful multiword queries; phrase/snippet support is desirable if size/performance permits.

## Likely implementation

Build a separate generated full-text search index during the Viewer workflow rather than bloating `conversations.json` with complete message bodies.

Candidate designs to benchmark:
1. per-conversation normalized unique token sets + multi-token intersection;
2. global inverted token -> conversation-ID postings index;
3. compact hashed postings / prefix index if corpus size requires it;
4. optional small snippets/message coordinates for result explanation without storing the full corpus twice.

Measure generated size, browser load time, query latency, and false-positive/false-negative behavior before selecting.

## QA

Regression tests should cover:
- a phrase/term present only in message body returns the conversation;
- title-only search continues to work;
- multiword body queries work predictably;
- hidden conversations and omitted curated message ranges do not leak through search;
- newly uploaded conversations enter the search index automatically;
- search index source IDs exactly match eligible Viewer catalog IDs.

## Related Viewer inclusion invariant

Separately from full-text search, every eligible non-quarantined conversation source should either appear in the Viewer or have an explicit machine-readable exclusion reason. The Viewer build must not silently depend on stale manifests.

[L2]   "content": "# Durable Project Documentation Convention

**Status:** ACTIVE coordination/infrastructure convention  
**Scope:** substantial repo-wide and cross-lane initiatives  
**Authority:** implements Nathan's 2026-09-13 Common directive to standardize project documentation and handoffs. This file is not a SAT/H(s)H theory surface.

## Purpose

Keep consequential work findable without turning Common into a second archive or proliferating one-off status files. A substantial initiative should normally leave three linked layers:

1. **Common notice / handoff** — concise routing entry saying what changed, who needs it, and where the durable record lives.
2. **Durable project/index home** — stable record of scope, status, outputs, provenance, dependencies, and access pointers.
3. **Navigation linkage** — Dashboard, README, index, catalog, or other appropriate front-door pointer when the initiative is important enough that future workers/users should discover it without searching Common history.

Small, local, temporary, or purely mechanical work does not need all three layers. Prefer updating an existing appropriate durable home over creating a new file.

## Minimum durable-home fields

A durable project/index home should make the following recoverable without reconstructing chat history:

- **Purpose / scope** — what the initiative covers and explicitly does not cover.
- **Status** — active, blocked, paused, superseded, complete, quarantined, historical, or another precise state.
- **Owner / lane** — current responsible workspace or process when meaningful.
- **Authority / epistemic type** — e.g. Nathan Direct, provenance/index infrastructure, Workshop, external-evidence lane, generated analysis; do not let location imply authority.
- **Source / provenance** — controlling directive/source pointers and, where available, raw IDs/timestamps; mark pending provenance rather than inventing it.
- **Outputs** — exact files, indexes, reports, workflows, datasets, or generated surfaces produced.
- **Dependencies / blockers** — what must happen before the next operation or promotion.
- **Access / navigation pointers** — canonical routes to the source material and outputs.
- **Supersession / history** — when definitions, methods, files, or status changed, preserve dated predecessor relationships instead of silently overwriting historical meaning.
- **Next operation** — concise restart point when the initiative is active.

## Common-room rule

Common is the routing layer, not the final record. A Common post for substantial work should be short and point to the durable home. Once an item stabilizes, update the Common entry or add a concise resolution pointer rather than appending repeated status chatter.

Recommended compact form:

`YYYY-MM-DD — FROM → TO/all — TYPE — subject — status/action — durable pointer`

## Navigation rule

Add a front-door link when at least one of these is true:

- the initiative is repo-wide or cross-lane;
- it changes how workers find or interpret project records;
- it defines an active operational convention;
- it creates a canonical glossary/index/catalog or other reusable retrieval surface;
- omission would make a future worker depend on Common archaeology to discover the current route.

Choose the narrowest appropriate navigation surface. Do not automatically add every project to the Dashboard; README/index linkage is often sufficient for infrastructure work.

## Provenance and epistemic safeguards

- Documentation is not promotion. Recording an interpretation, workshop result, quarantined item, or generated analysis does not make it canonical.
- Preserve authorship boundaries and source type.
- Mark present Nathan testimony separately from archive-corroborated historical material.
- Preserve superseded/historical definitions with dates and relationships when terminology evolves.
- Do not use worker consensus as a substitute for Nathan authorship, source evidence, or scientific validation.
- Private-resource paths are not public evidence surfaces; follow the Common repository-boundary rules for public-facing documentation.

## Generated-state rule

Do not hand-edit generated manifests/catalogs merely to make documentation appear current. Fix or run the owning generator/workflow, document the dependency, and verify the resulting artifact. If a generated surface has a temporary stale record but its consumer safely filters it, record the distinction between source-generation lag and consumer correctness.

## Initiative-specific application

### Historical definitions / glossary initiative

The repo-wide definitions initiative should use this convention:

- durable home: a canonical glossary/definitions index (location to be chosen by the owning documentation/tagging lane);
- each term should surface the current definition first while retaining dated earlier senses;
- record supersession, clarification, broader/narrower/related-standard-term relationships, and provenance;
- source definitions from verified Nathan-authored/tagged material and existing glossary/standard-to-SAT resources rather than generated reconstruction;
- Common should carry only coordination notices and links to the durable glossary/index.

### Autotag / tagging QA

Tagging QA should update a durable QA/index record with corpus coverage, selectivity behavior, known over-recall/under-recall, structural gaps, and tuning history. Common should carry only material changes or blockers.

### Viewer / catalog maintenance

Viewer/catalog QA should distinguish source-tree state, manifest state, generated catalog state, and publication/workflow state. Durable QA records should name the owning generator and verification criteria; Common should carry resolved handoffs or blockers.

## Relationship to existing Common rules

This convention implements and narrows the existing Common README rule: useful reusable information normally belongs in an appropriate durable README/index/workspace record, with a short Common pointer. It does not replace `GLASS_SAUSAGE_FACTORY_RECORD_POLICY.md`, epistemic/quarantine rules, or source-specific provenance ledgers.

[L2]   "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a compact sharded conversation-body search index for the public Viewer.

The index stores token -> conversation-number postings only; it does not duplicate
message bodies. Hidden conversations are absent because the input is the final Viewer
catalog. Partially curated conversations are indexed from their derived visible copy.
Public GLASS sources are read from the workflow's local GLASS checkout. Private
HSH_RESOURCES is never an input.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import build_conversation_viewer as viewer

TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\w+", re.UNICODE)


def normalize_for_tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    text = re.sub(r"h\s*\(\s*s\s*\)\s*h", "hsh", text, flags=re.I)
    return [t for t in (x.casefold() for x in TOKEN_RE.findall(text)) if len(t) >= 2]


def shard_key(token: str) -> str:
    first = token[0] if token else "_"
    return first if first in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789" else "_"


def catalog_sha(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def parse_companion_composite(text: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    # The browser uses a richer overlap merge. For conversation-level token search we
    # only need all visible dialogue text, so indexing the structured header plus the
    # labeled tail is sufficient and harmless if an overlap repeats tokens.
    marker = text.find("#########")
    start = text.find("{")
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if marker >= 0 and start >= 0 and marker > start:
        try:
            head = json.loads(text[start:marker].strip())
            messages.extend(viewer.normalize_conversation(head))
        except Exception:
            pass
        tail = text[marker + len("#########"):]
    else:
        tail = text
    for match in re.finditer(r"(?m)^\s*(Nathan|Srena)\s*$", tail):
        body_start = match.end()
        next_match = re.search(r"(?m)^\s*(?:Nathan|Srena)\s*$", tail[body_start:])
        body_end = body_start + next_match.start() if next_match else len(tail)
        body = tail[body_start:body_end].strip()
        if body:
            messages.append({"role": "user" if match.group(1) == "Nathan" else "companion", "speaker": match.group(1), "text": body})
    return messages


def source_text(convo: dict[str, Any], hsh_root: Path, glass_root: Path | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    if convo.get("curated"):
        raw = str(convo.get("raw_url") or "")
        if raw.startswith("http://") or raw.startswith("https://"):
            raise ValueError("curated conversation unexpectedly points to remote URL")
        path = hsh_root / "CONVERSATION_VIEWER" / raw
        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"), "json"

    source_repo = str(convo.get("source_repository") or "")
    if source_repo == "Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25":
        if glass_root is None:
            raise ValueError("GLASS checkout is required for external body indexing")
        rel = convo.get("source_path")
        if not rel:
            rel = convo.get("path")
            prefix = "SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/"
            rel = str(rel)[len(prefix):] if str(rel).startswith(prefix) else rel
        path = glass_root / str(rel)
    else:
        path = hsh_root / str(convo["path"])
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"), str(convo.get("parser") or "json")


def message_texts(convo: dict[str, Any], hsh_root: Path, glass_root: Path | None) -> list[str]:
    text, parser = source_text(convo, hsh_root, glass_root)
    if parser == "companion-composite":
        messages = parse_companion_composite(text)
    else:
        data = json.loads(text)
        messages = viewer.normalize_conversation(data)
    return [str(m.get("text") or "") for m in messages if str(m.get("text") or "").strip()]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--catalog", type=Path, default=Path("CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--hsh-root", type=Path, default=Path("."))
    ap.add_argument("--glass-root", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=Path("CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search"))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    hsh = args.hsh_root.resolve()
    glass = args.glass_root.resolve() if args.glass_root else None
    catalog_path = (hsh / args.catalog).resolve() if not args.catalog.is_absolute() else args.catalog
    catalog = json.loads(catalog_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    conversations = catalog.get("conversations")
    if not isinstance(conversations, list) or not conversations:
        ap.error("catalog has no conversations")

    postings: dict[str, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
    indexed = 0
    errors: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for index, convo in enumerate(conversations):
        try:
            tokens: set[str] = set()
            for text in message_texts(convo, hsh, glass):
                tokens.update(normalize_for_tokens(text))
            for token in tokens:
                postings[token].add(index)
            indexed += 1
        except Exception as exc:
            errors.append({"id": str(convo.get("id")), "path": str(convo.get("path")), "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"})

    if errors:
        raise RuntimeError(f"body index could not read {len(errors)} visible conversations; first errors: {errors[:5]}")

    out = (hsh / args.output_dir).resolve() if not args.output_dir.is_absolute() else args.output_dir
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    shards: dict[str, dict[str, list[int]]] = defaultdict(dict)
    for token in sorted(postings):
        shards[shard_key(token)][token] = sorted(postings[token])

    shard_meta = {}
    total_bytes = 0
    for key in sorted(shards):
        path = out / f"{key}.json"
        payload = {"schema_version": 1, "tokens": shards[key]}
        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        size = path.stat().st_size
        total_bytes += size
        shard_meta[key] = {"tokens": len(shards[key]), "bytes": size}

    meta = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "generated_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "catalog_sha256": catalog_sha(catalog_path),
        "conversation_ids": [str(c["id"]) for c in conversations],
        "conversation_count": len(conversations),
        "indexed_conversations": indexed,
        "unique_tokens": len(postings),
        "posting_count": sum(len(v) for v in postings.values()),
        "shard_bytes": total_bytes,
        "shards": shard_meta,
        "tokenization": "Unicode word tokens casefolded; H(s)H normalized to hsh; tokens shorter than 2 omitted",
        "privacy": "Final public Viewer catalog only; private HSH_RESOURCES is not indexed",
    }
    (out / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({k: meta[k] for k in ("conversation_count", "indexed_conversations", "unique_tokens", "posting_count", "shard_bytes")}, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

parts:
Yes — and your notes line up closely with the infrastructure that has appeared since we last discussed this.

The big new piece is that the Conversation Viewer now has genuine **full-body conversation search**, backed by a generated sharded inverted index rather than downloading every conversation. Meanwhile the archive has accumulated raw-window extractors, Nathan-direct packaging, layered autotagging through v3, priority-vocabulary tooling, conversation chronology, structural indexing, detailed folder-content indexing, and much stronger duplicate/branch/source-identity machinery. So we should reuse all of that rather than build another monolith.

What was still missing was exactly the interoperability layer you described: **general content search that can produce a durable, provenance-bearing topical index.** I created the first version:

`tools/search_archive_content.py`  
Commit: `d161b648b0ce5d62a5dcbc41f9d941a782cc0ef2`

It searches raw conversation JSON message-by-message, arbitrary JSON scalar-by-scalar, and TXT/MD/CSV/YAML/code/etc. line-by-line; it can also extract existing PDF text when `pypdf` is available, without OCR. It supports topic aliases and emits both machine-readable JSON and a human-readable Markdown index.

The output model now includes essentially your requested fields: topic/aliases; conversation title/CID/date when available; speaker/role; message ID or other locator; exact excerpt; source SHA-256; candidate proposal/derivation/correction/failed-branch/supersession/unresolved signals; related indexed topics; Viewer pointer where resolvable; and a “why this hit matters” field. It also generates a lightweight co-occurrence concept graph.

Crucially, I built in a distinction I think matters a lot for what you want: **the machine may detect a supersession signal, but it may not declare something superseded.** Actual chains such as

`first appearance → elaboration → reuse → correction → supersession`

need to be constructed from the chronological source record. That prevents the index from quietly becoming an AI-authored history of SAT.

And your example is perfect for the first real test:

`dimensional anchor → constants network → star-shaped derivation → cross-sector holdout → closure`

I want that to be the first bounded topic configuration, because it simultaneously tests alias retrieval, obscure terminology, chronology, conceptual adjacency, and whether the concept graph recovers something more useful than simple keyword search.

One qualification: the file is committed, but I have **not yet called the script runtime-green**. The available execution container couldn't fetch the new GitHub file for a local `py_compile`, so the next operation is to execute it through a repo-native runtime, fix anything mechanical, and then generate the first actual `indexes/topical/` JSON + Markdown pair from that five-concept chain.

I’ve recorded all of this as Mercer Run 133, including exactly what existing infrastructure I found and why this tool is complementary rather than duplicative. memcite
And ideally, we include boolean capability, with "NEAR" including adjustable windows and sort by author

Yes. I’d add those as first-class query features rather than trying to fake them in post-processing:

- Boolean expressions: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, and quoted phrases.
- `NEAR`: e.g. `"star-shaped" NEAR/5 derivation`, with the window adjustable in words/tokens; probably also a message-level proximity mode.
- Author/speaker filtering: `author:Nathan`, `author:assistant`, named companion/agent where preserved.
- Sorting/grouping by author, with secondary chronology sorting.
- Ideally field filters too: `title:`, `topic:`, `status:`, `conversation:`, `date:`, etc.

For the index output, I’d preserve the query that produced each hit and the actual NEAR distance where applicable. That makes the search reproducible rather than merely producing a pile of matches.

I’d also make **author grouping distinct from authorship authority**: sorting by Nathan versus assistant is mechanical; determining whether quoted/embedded material is genuinely Nathan-authored remains provenance work.

That moves this from a grep-like archive scanner toward a small corpus-query language, which is much more appropriate for 350+ conversations. memcite
And date sorting and whatever bells and whistles allow really robust transparent searchability.

Absolutely. I’d treat the target as a small, transparent archive search engine rather than a glorified grep.

Beyond Boolean + adjustable `NEAR/n`, I’d want chronological ascending/descending sorting, date/range filters, author/speaker sorting and filtering, conversation/date grouping, exact phrase and regex modes, case-sensitive/insensitive options, alias expansion, fielded queries, exclusion filters, hit counts, context-window controls, and deterministic ranking.

More importantly, every result should remain auditable back to source: exact path, conversation UUID, message ID, speaker, timestamp, source hash, raw locator, Viewer locator, matched terms, actual proximity distance, query expression, and enough surrounding context to understand why it matched. Results should be exportable as JSON/JSONL, Markdown, CSV/TSV, and probably plain text.

For chronology specifically, I’d support both simple `--sort date` and **topic timelines**. A topic timeline should distinguish first known occurrence, subsequent occurrences, dense development periods, corrections, explicit reversals/supersession signals, and latest known occurrence—without automatically declaring conceptual supersession merely from dates.

There are some particularly useful bells and whistles worth building toward: fuzzy spelling tolerance; stemming/lemmatization as an optional expansion rather than silently changing queries; wildcard/prefix search; Unicode normalization; configurable stopwords; result deduplication that understands our exact/metadata/subset/branch families; saved named queries; query-result manifests; concept co-occurrence matrices; conversation-to-conversation links; topic-to-topic adjacency; and perhaps a `--history TOPIC` mode expressly designed to reconstruct:

`first appearance → elaboration → derivation/use → correction → later state`

I’d also include a very useful **explain-search mode**. Given a result, it should be able to say mechanically:

> matched alias X at tokens 143–145; Y occurred 7 tokens later; passed `NEAR/10`; author filter matched `user`; source date 2025-…; duplicate-family relation = subset/superset; displayed state retained because no authority inference was requested.

That degree of transparency will matter enormously when we're excavating things like the star-shaped derivation map and trying to distinguish “couldn’t find it” from “it isn't there.”

So yes: rather than incrementally bolting flags onto Run 133 forever, I’d now regard **robust transparent corpus search + reproducible topical/provenance indexing** as the design target. The Viewer search remains the fast human front end; this becomes the workers’ excavation instrument and the generator for durable indexes. memcite
Alright... lets do it

I’m upgrading the Run-133 tool rather than starting over. I’ll make the query language explicit and inspectable: Boolean/parentheses, quoted phrases, `NEAR/n`, field filters, author/date controls, deterministic sorting/grouping, context controls, and provenance-rich JSON/JSONL/Markdown/CSV outputs. Then I’ll validate it on synthetic records before pointing it at the archive.
